title: SDK parity audit – working notes (auth/retry/timeouts/streaming)
linked_artifacts: Jira: SUP-29410 (python streaming timeouts not honored)
content:
Context
- This is the “raw notes” doc we use while auditing code + reproducing support issues. Expect incomplete thoughts.
- Goal: identify current mismatches across Python/TS/Go; propose consistent standard; track concrete fixes + PRs.

Owner map
- DRI: Monica Patel
- Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan (me)
- Language owners: Sabrina (Python), Dana (TS), Mateusz (Go)
- Partners: Marcus (security), Allison/Sean (SRE/reliability), Logan/Nadia (telemetry)

Quick links (threads we keep coming back to)
- Kickoff: Slack #devex (1767472305)
- Default timeouts debate: Slack #devex (1767579921)
- Retryable status codes/network errors: Slack #devex (1767685544)
- Streaming disconnects behind corp proxy: Slack #devex (1767789012)
- Auth env var naming + secret redaction: Slack #eng-security (1767873008)
- Retry storm / load impact: Slack #eng-sre (1768014202)

Support drivers we’re trying to kill
- SUP-29410: Python streaming requests appear to ignore configured timeouts.
- SUP-29438: TS SDK retries on 400 (customer saw duplicates, billing concerns).
- SUP-29477: Go SDK ignores Retry-After on 429; retries too quickly.
- SUP-29505: Streaming disconnects behind proxy; no guidance; hard to surface request_id / partial output.
- INT-1182: request_id not visible in SDK errors.


=== A) Audit findings by topic ===

A1) Authentication resolution + env vars
Current behavior (as of audit week 1; verify in code as PRs land)
- Python
  - Observed: constructor param api_key supported.
  - Env var: historically REDWOOD_API_KEY (confirmed) and some examples using REDWOOD_TOKEN (?)
  - Potential mismatch: precedence when both constructor + env set (should prefer explicit param).
  - Failure mode: error messages sometimes include “provided key …” risk (needs redaction policy).
- TypeScript
  - Observed: reads process.env; older name REDWOOD_KEY seen in a few examples.
  - Precedence: unclear whether explicit option overrides env in all call paths (esp. when client factory wraps).
  - Risk: debug logging may include headers if user sets verbose fetch logging.
- Go
  - Observed: options struct supports APIKey string; environment fallback exists.
  - Precedence: looked correct in main client constructor; but streaming helper uses a separate http client builder (double check same auth resolution).

Desired standard (draft)
- Resolution order: explicit client option (api_key / bearer_token) > env vars (preferred names) > error.
- Supported env vars (final names; to be aligned with security doc):
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY (primary)
  - REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN (secondary, if we support bearer explicitly)
  - REDWOOD_BASE_URL (optional)
- Deprecations
  - REDWOOD_TOKEN / REDWOOD_KEY if present in old SDKs: accept temporarily w/ deprecation warning (do NOT document).
- Header format
  - API key: Authorization: Bearer <key> (confirm w/ platform; historically some used X-API-Key)
  - NOTE: platform partner says gateway will consistently accept Bearer; any X-API-Key should be treated as legacy and phased out.

Action items
- Python: PR #842 aligns env var names + precedence + redaction-safe errors.
- TS: PR #1316 aligns env vars + precedence; add deprecation warnings.
- Go: PR #630 aligns env vars + header format; ensure secrets not logged.
- Add conformance tests:
  - “explicit overrides env”
  - “deprecated env var accepted but warns (if we keep this behavior)”
  - “error message does not echo secret”

Open questions
- Do we support BOTH API key and bearer token as different concepts, or is everything a “key” that uses Bearer? (Security review leaning towards: treat as one, keep naming consistent; we can still accept REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN if it exists internally.)


A2) Retries / backoff / Retry-After
Observed inconsistencies
- Retryable codes
  - Python: retries 429 and some 5xx; unclear on 408/409/425/502/503/504 (needs standard list).
  - TS: at least one path retried on 400 due to middleware “retry on any non-2xx” bug (SUP-29438).
  - Go: retries 429/5xx but ignores Retry-After header (SUP-29477); backoff too aggressive.
- Network errors
  - Python httpx: connect/read timeouts show up as exceptions; we need consistent mapping to retryable.
  - TS fetch: aborted requests / ECONNRESET behave differently across node versions; needs explicit handling.
  - Go net/http: context cancellation should not trigger retries (user intentionally cancelled).
- Jitter/backoff
  - Python: exponential backoff exists but jitter formula differs from TS.
  - TS: added jitter in PR #1307; but verify it matches “full jitter” vs “equal jitter”.
  - Go: uses time.Sleep and increments attempt; initial delay differs.
- Retry-After
  - Python: parsing supports seconds; date format uncertain.
  - TS: PR #1307 added parsing seconds/date; verify both.
  - Go: PR #612 adds parsing; verify “date” format not just ints.

Draft standard (from SRE + DevEx discussion)
- Retryable HTTP status codes:
  - 408, 409 (ONLY if safe; for our API, 409 used for “conflict” rarely; default maybe OFF), 425 (optional), 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
  - Non-retryable: 400, 401, 403, 404, 422.
- Network errors:
  - Retry on: connection reset, TLS handshake errors, temporary DNS, EOF mid-response (non-streaming), read timeout.
  - Do NOT retry on: explicit user abort/cancel, context cancelled, request body serialization errors.
- Attempts:
  - Max attempts default: 3 (meaning 1 initial + 2 retries) or 4? Pending final. SRE preference: keep conservative to avoid thundering herd.
- Backoff:
  - Exponential backoff with jitter.
  - Respect Retry-After if present and parseable; cap to max_delay.

Notes from #eng-sre thread (1768014202)
- Rollout risk: changing defaults can cause retry storms during 429 incidents.
- Mitigation: keep low attempts; include randomized jitter; add client-side “retry budget” per request; and ensure we never retry streaming by default.

Action items
- Python: PR #846 standardize retry defaults + Retry-After parse.
- TS: PR #1298 fixes retry middleware classification; PR #1307 Retry-After + jitter.
- Go: PR #612 standardize policy + Retry-After.
- Platform: gateway PR #28411 ensures Retry-After on 429 consistently.

Open questions
- 409: should we include by default? (We need to understand our API behavior; Henry says 409 is rare, usually indicates misconfig not transient.)
- Retry on 408: safe, but watch for proxies generating 408.


A3) Timeout model
Observed inconsistencies
- Python
  - Reports from SUP-29410: streaming ignores configured timeout. Likely using httpx timeout incorrectly or not applied to streaming iter.
  - Mixed: some calls use “timeout=30” overall; others have connect/read defaults.
- TypeScript
  - Node fetch timeouts are typically via AbortController; streaming requires different wiring.
  - Some timeouts apply only to request start, not to full stream duration (customers interpret “timeout” as overall).
- Go
  - Using context deadlines (best) but some streaming reads do not honor context cancellation consistently.

Draft decision direction (from internal ADR discussions)
- Support both overall request timeout and granular connect/read.
- Default overall timeout should be long enough for streaming (or streaming uses “no overall by default but has idle/read timeout”).
- Provide a consistent configuration surface:
  - timeout_ms (overall)
  - connect_timeout_ms
  - read_timeout_ms (or “response_timeout_ms”)
- Streaming nuance:
  - “overall timeout” in streaming might kill long generations; maybe set default overall = None for streaming, but enforce idle timeout.

Action items
- Python: PR #850 implements connect/read/overall mapping.
- TS: PR #1302 abort plumbing for streaming vs non-streaming.
- Go: PR #619 aligns timeouts + context cancellation.

Open questions
- What is the default overall timeout for streaming? If we set 60s overall, long responses fail unexpectedly. If we set none, customers can hang forever behind proxies. Proposal: streaming defaults to (connect=10s, read/idle=60s, overall=disabled) but documented.


A4) Streaming semantics + disconnect handling
Streaming failure modes we’ve seen
- Corporate proxy buffering + unexpected FIN mid-chunk (Slack #devex 1767789012)
- Half-closed connections: server closes write end but client still reading.
- HTTP2 stream reset.
- Idle read timeouts causing disconnect.

Key parity issues
- Partial output
  - Python: sometimes yields tokens/events and then raises generic exception without attaching partial text; unclear where partial resides.
  - TS: some examples treat stream as “all or nothing”; cancellation path doesn’t surface partial safely.
  - Go: streaming returns an iterator; on error, request_id missing in some errors.
- Retry guidance
  - We should not auto-retry streaming by default (duplicate partial outputs, potential double charging confusion).
  - Provide recommended pattern: log request_id; if disconnect occurs after first chunk, treat as partial; ask customer to retry with idempotency key if they must.

Desired behavior
- On stream disconnect, raise a typed StreamingError (name varies per language but consistent fields):
  - request_id (if known)
  - status_code (if known)
  - retryable boolean (false by default for mid-stream)
  - streaming_disconnect_reason (enum-ish string: "eof", "timeout", "reset", "proxy", "cancelled") best-effort
  - partial_output (where feasible)
- Ensure request_id propagation in both headers + event stream where possible.

Action items
- Python: PR #854 streaming disconnect handling + typed errors.
- TS: PR #1311 cancellation + partial output semantics.
- Go: PR #624 streaming error types + reconnect guidance.
- Platform: PR #28426 standardize request_id propagation.

Open questions
- How to represent partial output consistently? Options:
  - Provide partial text buffer on error object (risk: memory for long streams).
  - Provide “events consumed so far” count, and user can build their own buffer.
  - Current proposal: include partial_text up to a capped size (e.g., last 32KB) + token count.


A5) Error taxonomy + typed errors
Observed issues
- request_id often missing (INT-1182).
- Error classes differ wildly; TS has a generic APIError but fields not stable.
- Some SDKs expose raw response body; others swallow it.

Desired taxonomy (shared concept)
- Base error fields across SDKs:
  - message
  - request_id
  - status_code
  - error_code (string enum from gateway)
  - retryable (boolean)
  - retry_after_ms (if present)
- Named types
  - AuthenticationError (401/403)
  - RateLimitError (429)
  - TimeoutError (client-side)
  - NetworkError (client-side)
  - ServerError (5xx)
  - StreamingError (stream disconnect)

Action items
- Linear ENG-5126: define shared taxonomy + conformance “golden” error shapes.
- Platform: PR #28440 error_code enum for SDK consumption.


A6) Telemetry/logging fields
We likely cannot auto-collect telemetry for all customers (privacy/enterprise). But we can:
- Standardize logging hooks + fields (if user enables) and ensure they can pull these into their observability.
Fields requested by Support/SRE
- request_id
- sdk_language + sdk_version
- retry_count / attempt
- timeout_ms (effective)
- retry_after_ms (if used)
- streaming_disconnect_reason
- http_status_code

Action items
- Linear ENG-5129: add standardized fields/hook interface.


=== B) Repro scripts / minimal tests ===

B1) Retry-After 429 parsing test
Goal: ensure all SDKs respect Retry-After in both formats.

Server behavior (simulated fixture)
- Respond 429 with headers:
  - Retry-After: 2
  - x-request-id: req_test_429_seconds
- Respond 429 with headers:
  - Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT
  - x-request-id: req_test_429_date

Python (pseudo)
- Configure max_attempts=2, base_delay=0.1, max_delay=5
- Assert delay >= 2s for first case
- Assert delay approx (date-now) (capped) for second case

TS (pseudo)
- Use fake timers; assert backoff uses parsed Retry-After rather than exponential.

Go (pseudo)
- Use httptest server and capture timestamps; assert sleep >= expected.


B2) TS retries on 400 regression
- Setup fixture returns 400 with error_code=INVALID_REQUEST
- Ensure SDK does NOT retry and returns terminal error with retryable=false
- Reference: SUP-29438


B3) Python streaming timeout honored
- Fixture streams a token every 10s; set read/idle timeout 2s -> expect TimeoutError
- Fixture streams tokens normally but never ends; set overall timeout 5s -> expect overall timeout
- Reference: SUP-29410


B4) request_id included in errors
- Fixture returns 500 with x-request-id req_test_500
- Ensure error has request_id across all SDKs
- Also verify request_id present on streaming early error (e.g., 401 before stream begins)


=== C) Running mismatch list (rolling) ===

Legend
- P0 = must fix before stable release
- P1 = should fix in v1 standard rollout
- P2 = follow-up

1) Auth env var precedence mismatch (explicit vs env)
- Priority: P0
- Status: in-flight
- Owners: Sabrina (py), Dana (ts), Mateusz (go)
- Notes: ensure no secret echoing; confirm legacy env var behavior
- PRs: py#842, ts#1316, go#630

2) Retry classification retries on 400 (TS)
- Priority: P0
- Status: fixed pending release
- Owner: Dana
- Notes: caused duplicate requests concerns (SUP-29438)
- PR: ts#1298

3) Retry-After ignored (Go)
- Priority: P0
- Status: in review
- Owner: Mateusz
- Notes: SUP-29477; also depends on gateway consistently emitting Retry-After (platform PR #28411)
- PR: go#612

4) Python streaming timeouts not honored
- Priority: P0
- Status: in progress
- Owner: Sabrina
- Notes: likely due to httpx streaming iterator not applying read timeout; reproduce with slow token stream
- PR: py#850 + py#854

5) request_id missing in SDK errors (all)
- Priority: P0
- Status: partially resolved
- Owner: Ibrahim (taxonomy) + platform partner Ethan
- Notes: platform PR #28426 ensures request_id propagation; SDKs need to parse header consistently

6) Default timeout values inconsistent
- Priority: P1
- Status: pending ADR
- Owner: Ibrahim + Allison
- Notes: need final defaults and how we message in migration guide

7) Streaming disconnect: typed error + partial output semantics
- Priority: P1
- Status: in progress
- Owners: all language owners
- Notes: keep conservative on retry; document idempotency guidance

8) Error taxonomy fields not stable
- Priority: P1
- Status: drafting
- Owner: Ibrahim
- Notes: needs platform error_code enum (PR #28440)

9) Telemetry/logging fields inconsistent
- Priority: P2
- Status: not started
- Owner: Logan + Nadia


=== D) Notes from code reading (grab bag) ===

Python
- Found multiple timeout config entry points (client init vs per-request). Need one story.
- Ensure redaction: never log Authorization header in debug logs.

TypeScript
- Some middleware chain order issues: retry runs before auth in one factory? verify.
- AbortController usage differs between streaming and non-streaming.

Go
- Context cancellation: ensure we return context.Canceled without retry.
- Streaming reader should stop on ctx.Done promptly.


=== E) Next steps / TODO (weekly) ===

Week of 2026-02-17
- [ ] Confirm final retryable status code set with SRE (Allison/Sean) and publish standard.
- [ ] Finish conformance fixtures for 429/Retry-After and 400 no-retry.
- [ ] Validate request_id appears in:
  - non-streaming 4xx/5xx
  - streaming preflight errors
  - mid-stream disconnect errors (best-effort)
- [ ] Draft migration notes focusing on behavior changes:
  - retries defaults
  - timeout model
  - env var changes (deprecated names)


Appendix: naming conventions we’re leaning toward (not final)
- Options
  - max_attempts
  - initial_backoff_ms
  - max_backoff_ms
  - timeout_ms
  - connect_timeout_ms
  - read_timeout_ms
  - retry_on (advanced)
- Error fields
  - request_id
  - status_code
  - error_code
  - retryable
  - retry_after_ms
  - retry_count

(End)
